evidence_strength.5.1.2.1: collected from Microsoft Graph /beta (users/{id}/authentication/requirements); CIS marks this control Manual and documents no automated procedure
evidence_strength.5.2.2.x: the 5.2.2 Conditional Access controls are evaluated from the policies Graph returns. CIS documents them as Entra portal steps and names no cmdlet, so these reach the benchmark's answer by a path it does not describe.

sections_evaluated.name: Microsoft Entra admin center

evidence_strength.6.1.2: sampled -- 0 of at most 0 mailboxes inspected; the control is about configuration, but a clean result does not prove every mailbox

sections_evaluated.name: Exchange admin center
violations: CIS 6.1.1: Exchange Online facts were not collected, so whether AuditDisabled is organizationally False could not be established -- section 6 was not evaluated (this is not a pass)

evidence_strength.section: collected with Get-PnPTenant, not the Get-SPOTenant the benchmark documents -- Microsoft.Online.SharePoint.PowerShell is Windows-only and cannot run in a Linux execution environment. The same CSOM tenant properties are read.

sections_evaluated.name: SharePoint admin center
violations: CIS 7.2.1: SharePoint tenant facts were not collected, so whether modern authentication is required could not be established -- section 7 was not evaluated (this is not a pass)

evidence_strength.section: collected with the cmdlets CIS documents (Get-CsTeamsClientConfiguration, Get-CsTenantFederationConfiguration, Get-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy, Get-CsTeamsMessagingPolicy), all verified present in the execution environment. Meeting and messaging policies are evaluated across ALL policies, not only Global, because a permissive non-global policy still governs the users it is assigned to.

sections_evaluated.name: Microsoft Teams admin center
violations: CIS 8.1.1: Teams facts were not collected, so whether external file sharing is limited to approved cloud storage services could not be established -- section 8 was not evaluated (this is not a pass)

evidence_strength.section: collected from the Fabric admin API. CIS documents these as portal steps plus a CIS-supplied helper function; the API returns the same tenantSettings the portal displays. A setting that is enabled but scoped to named security groups is treated as restricted, which is what the benchmark accepts.

sections_evaluated.name: Microsoft Fabric
violations: CIS 9.1.1: Fabric tenant settings were not collected, so whether guest user access is restricted could not be established -- section 9 was not evaluated (this is not a pass)
